COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPMS No.1546 of 2023
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Raman Kumar Shah, Advocate, for 
the petitioners.
The petitioner before this Court is an 
employer, who has put a challenge to the award 
dated 25.02.2023, as it has been rendered by the 
learned Industrial Tribunal/Labour Court, 
Dehradun, in Adjudication Case No.71 of 2008, 
“Jayanti Prasad Benjwal Vs. Secretary, 
G.M.O.U, Kotdwar”, by virtue of the impugned 
award, the employee has been directed to be 
reinstated and 25% of the arrears has been 
directed to be paid. The Presiding Officer by 
the award dated 25.02.2023, has held that the 
order of the termination of the services of the 
workman on 29.08.2006, was bad in the eyes of 
law.
Issue notices to the respondent. The steps 
to be taken by the petitioner within a period of 
one week from today.
List after service of the notice on the 
respondent.
The execution of the award dated 
25.02.2023, would be kept in abeyance, subject 
to the condition, that the petitioner/employer 
reinstate the respondent into the services  forthwith, but so far as the payment of the 
arrears as determined by the Presiding 
Officer/Labour Court is concerned, that would 
be kept in abeyance, and would abide by the 
decision on the writ petition. 
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 25.05.2023
NR/

06.06.2023 WPMS No. 1550 of 2023 
With
WPMS No. 1546 of 2023
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Raman Kumar Shah, Advocate, 
for the applicants.
Mr. B.D. Upadhyay, Senior 
Advocate, assisted by Mr. Mayank Pandey, 
Advocate, for the respondent.
The issue involved in the present 
writ petition almost happens to be akin to 
that as engages consideration in Writ 
Petition (M/S) No. 1546 of 2023.
By virtue of an award dated 
25.02.2023, as rendered in Adjudication 
Case No. 70 of 2008, Anil Chandola Vs. 
Secretary, G.M.O.U. Kotdwar, whereby the 
reference under Section 4A of the U.P. 
Industrial Disputes Act, was sought to be 
adjudicated as against the order of 
termination dated 07.09.2006. 
The said reference has been 
answered by the learned labour Court by 
the impugned award, by virtue of which the 
workman has been directed to be reinstated 
along with 25% of the back wages to be paid 
to him. 
In the connected writ petition, this 
Court has stayed the effect and operation of 
the award subject to the condition that the 
workman would be reinstated. So far as the  payment of arrears of 25% of the back 
wages is concerned, that was directed to be 
kept in abeyance.
Hence, this writ petition would too 
carry a similar interim order as that passed 
on 25.05.2023 in Writ Petition (M/S) No. 
1546 of 2023.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 06.06.2023
Mahinder/
